summary_text: Across four independent dates in May 2026, the user placed orders on three weekdays and one weekend. Daypart behavior was distributed across night, morning, and evening, with no single daypart dominating. The most consistent category combination observed was Fruits and Milk, appearing on two independent dates (2026-05-27 and 2026-05-31). Other categories (Chocolates, Cookies Biscuits, Washing Powder, Washing Bar, Chips) appeared only on single dates. No durable routines or high-confidence preferences can be established due to the limited repetition of specific items or broad category sets outside of the Fruits/Milk pair.
shopping_need_text: The recurring combination of Fruits and Milk suggests a basic need for fresh produce and dairy, potentially for breakfast or light snacking. Other purchases indicate isolated needs for snacks (Chocolates, Cookies Biscuits, Chips) and household cleaning supplies (Washing Powder, Washing Bar).
uncertainty_text: Analysis is based on four independent dates. Only the Fruits and Milk combination has sufficient repetition (2 dates) to support medium confidence. All other category observations are isolated to single dates, preventing inference of stable preferences or routines for those items. Daypart and day-type patterns are sparse and do not indicate a strong habitual bias.
